decisions.reason: As a newly launched core safety-shoe line in the firm’s main business, it is still an unresolved option with meaningful strategic fit, so despite the cost of carrying several models the firm is more likely to keep it for another year.

This comfort insole complements the footwear range and likely has relatively low carrying cost, so even with modest website prominence and overlap with other insoles the option value still favors keeping it.

The supportive insole is a low-cost adjacent product whose market potential is not yet fully resolved, but its similarity to other insole offerings makes it somewhat more droppable than the firm’s more distinctive launches.

The ergonomic safety-shoe series received its own page and fits the firm’s innovation-led positioning in protective footwear, so management would likely preserve this option while demand information continues to emerge.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a more specialized and potentially costlier niche line, but they remain close to the firm’s protective-footwear capabilities and are likely worth retaining until their value becomes clearer.

Because the moulded insole was highlighted on the home page and presented as a flagship direction, management is very unlikely to withdraw it so soon given its strategic signaling role and probably low carrying cost.
